content.user_title: Audit Java Projects for DDD Compliance
content.value_statement: Java architecture can drift across layers, dependencies, and domain models. This skill reviews recent changes or entire projects against practical DDD rules.
actual_capabilities: Selects incremental or full-project review mode from the requested scope.
Finds changed Java files with Git for focused pre-commit reviews.
Discovers production Java files for full architecture audits.
Checks package placement, naming, base classes, dependencies, and exception handling.
Identifies anemic models and other documented DDD anti-patterns.
Produces prioritized violations with rule references and suggested fixes.
limitations: The rules target the supplied Java architecture conventions, not every valid DDD implementation.
Repository discovery requires Git, find, grep, and a compatible shell environment.
The skill reviews source structure but does not compile code or execute tests.
Intentional architecture exceptions still require confirmation from project maintainers.

use_cases.title: Review a Feature Branch
use_cases.description: Check changed Java files before commit and receive focused DDD violations with practical fixes.

use_cases.title: Audit Layer Boundaries
use_cases.description: Evaluate dependencies, package placement, domain behavior, and exception boundaries across a complete project.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Architecture Work
use_cases.description: Use severity-ranked findings and layer scores to plan remediation across teams and releases.

prompt_templates.title: Check Recent Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Check my changed Java files for DDD compliance. Report only violations, cite the relevant rule, and provide a specific fix.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of staged or unstaged work

prompt_templates.title: Review One Layer
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the {layer} layer in {project_path}. Check package placement, naming, base classes, dependencies, and exception handling.
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused review of one architecture layer

prompt_templates.title: Run a Full Architecture Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a full DDD compliance audit of this Java project. Score each layer, identify cross-layer violations, and rank remediation work by severity.

prompt_templates.title: Trace an Aggregate Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the {aggregate_name} workflow end to end. Trace dependencies across layers, detect anemic modeling, and evaluate transaction and exception boundaries.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of behavior spanning multiple layers

output_examples.input: Check my staged Java changes for DDD compliance.
output: High: The domain service imports an infrastructure mapper, which reverses the allowed dependency direction.
Fix: Depend on a domain repository interface and move the mapper access into the infrastructure implementation.

output_examples.input: Run a full DDD audit and summarize the weakest layer.
output_examples.output: The domain layer has the lowest compliance score. Its main issues are public identity setters, anemic aggregates, and infrastructure dependencies.

output_examples.input: Review the order application layer and suggest priorities.
output: Critical: Remove direct infrastructure dependencies from application services.
High: Move business invariants from orchestration services into the order aggregate.
Medium: Rename query methods to express clear intent.

best_practices: State whether the review should cover changed files, one layer, or the entire project.
Provide project-specific base classes, naming rules, and approved architecture exceptions.
Verify high-severity findings against source context before scheduling remediation.
anti_patterns: Do not apply the supplied Java conventions unchanged to unrelated languages or architectures.
Do not treat a compliance score as proof of runtime correctness or complete domain modeling.
Do not request an incremental review when unchanged project files must also be evaluated.

faq.question: Does this skill modify source files?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflow reads source files and repository diffs, then returns a review report.

faq.question: Which languages does it support?
faq.answer: Its rules, discovery commands, and examples target Java projects.

faq.question: What is the difference between incremental and full mode?
faq.answer: Incremental mode checks changed Java files. Full mode reviews all production Java files and cross-layer relationships.

faq.question: Does it support every Java framework?
faq.answer: No. It follows supplied layered conventions and uses MyBatis-style examples. Adapt project-specific names and base classes before accepting findings.

faq.question: Can I use it in continuous integration?
faq.answer: You can invoke it during review workflows, but the skill does not include a standalone continuous integration setup.

faq.question: How should I interpret the compliance score?
faq.answer: Use it to prioritize review. Confirm each violation against business intent and approved project exceptions.
